newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks slip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks slip on profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended slightly lower Tuesday on profit-taking after two straight sessions of large gains, but an inflation warning by a senior central banker rekindled fears that the Federal Reserve may be ready to raise interest rates.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended off 6.66 points at 5,727.18 after gaining a total of 127 points on Monday and Friday. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,145 to 1,137 on active volume of 371 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said the market's bullish tone in the wake of Friday's August payrolls report, which allayed Wall Street's worst inflation fears, was dampened by Fed Gov. Janet Yellen's comment that the economy was at a critical point.
"We're in an inflationary danger zone," Yellen told Reuters in an interview. "There's definitely a chance inflation will rise."

Her cautious comments suggested that she might be willing to support a small, quarter percentage point rise in short-term interest rates at the Fed's next policy-making meeting on Sept. 24 to help ensure against higher inflation.

Such a move, if it occurred, would be the first rate rise by the central bank in about 1-1/2 years and would be designed to head off a rise in inflation that could jeopardise the 5-1/2-year-old economic expansion.

The inflation-sensitive bond market fell, with the 30-year Treasury bond off nearly half of a point, and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction to its price, up to 7.11 percent from Monday's close of 7.07 percent.
Analysts said they were impressed with the stock market's performance, noting that investors have been pricing in a rise in short-term interest rates after a series of strong economic reports.
"Stocks have rallied in the past two days. So far this first day of a pullback looks awfully good given what's happening to bonds," said Ralph Bloch, chief technical analyst at Raymond James.

The latest indication of the economy's overall strength came on Friday with news that the jobless rate fell to 5.1 percent in August -- its lowest level in nearly 7-1/2 years -- as the economy created 250,000 jobs.
The concern is that as the economy moves towards the so-called full employment, workers will be able to push harder for wage increases.
Bloch said the market still faced key reports this week.
"We have the Beige Book tomorrow, producer prices Thursday and consumer prices Friday. If the numbers are benign I think this market goes higher," he said.
The Beige Book is the Fed's account of its view of the economy.

Among the big movers, ITT Corp. lost 7-7/8 or 14 percent of its value at 48-1/8 after it warned that its quarterly results will be below Wall Street's expectations because of weak revenues from its casinos.

Ford Motor Co. lost 3/8 to 31-5/8. It said its Latin American operations will suffer a loss in the second half that will be roughly twice as large as the region's first-half loss of $130 million. Brazil makes up the largest portion of Ford's Latin American operations.

General Motors Corp., which also has substantial Brazilian operations, was down 3/8 to 47-7/8. Chrysler Corp. fell 1/2 to 28-1/4. It recently announced plans to spend $315 million for its first Brazilian assembly plant.

International Business Machines Corp. was up 1/2 to 118-1/8 after IBM said strong customer demand for its new models of mainframe computers has been so strong that it may sell out all it can produce this year.
Praegitzer Industries Inc., a circuit board maker, tumbled 26 percent or 3-8/16 to 9-13/16 on an earnings warning.
Gap Inc. rose 1-1/4 to 31-5/8 after Goldman Sachs upgraded the retailer.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 0.72 of a point to 1,149.43.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 0.05 to 663.81. The American Stock Exchange index was up 3.27 to 565.23.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.21 to 356.49. The average share was up 3 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,522.109 up 6.598 or 0.10 percent.
